On Windows, FastAPI TestClient uses a loopback socketpair emulation; a blanket socket guard flags it as network use. With a loopback-aware guard all tests pass with external network blocked, so BRD-004 holds.

findings.resolution: Scoped to the revision and subject_revision keys. The approval declaration's own expires_at was verified untouched in both contracts.
findings.summary: --sync-contracts replaced any git:<sha> anywhere in the contract, context-free, so a field intentionally holding a superseded revision could be rewritten.

findings.resolution: Replaced with AST call-expression detection covering os.system, os.popen, os.exec*, os.spawn*, os.posix_spawn and pty. Regression test added.
findings.summary: The bounded_external_adapter check contained dead code: 'and banned == "subprocess"' made the os.system and pty branches unreachable, so only a bare subprocess import was ever detected.
check_security.py's own secret scan skips .nornyx/ and evidence/; mitigated because validate_repository.py scans the full tree in the same gate pipeline.
.nornyx/contracts/evidence/ is intentionally not gitignored: governance evidence must be committed because the contracts bind it by sha256. Contents confirmed free of secrets.

Demonstration limitations, not vulnerabilities: no authentication on the API with 0.0.0.0 binding; no rate limiting or request-size ceiling; the client-supplied risk field selects the authorization tier without server-side re-derivation, which is inert today because the gated action is a fixed inert stub.

reviews.summary: PASS in all three rounds. No committed secrets, no shell injection, cloned repository content never executed, and no fabricated or overstated assurance claim. Round 3 probed the evaluation-time repair adversarially: naive and malformed time pins, oversized and non-UTF-8 contract content, revision injection via environment override, approval-expiry tampering, and P7D bypass. Reviewer is read-only and did not modify the implementation.
